summary: Full E2E test of System Maintenance / Outage Tracker feature. Backend: 11/11 pytest tests pass (public status endpoint no-auth, admin gating 401 without token, partial-update preserves other fields, threshold clamped to [5,600], manual toggle reflects publicly, incidents endpoint schema). Frontend: admin /admin/maintenance page loads with saved values, message/window/threshold persist across reload, toggle ON/OFF works with correct button labels, admin/founder bypass works (logged-in admin sees /dashboard normally with manual ON), anonymous incognito visit to `/` shows branded 'Scheduled Maintenance' overlay with correct message + window, /login and /signup remain accessible (exempt) while manual ON — admin can always sign back in, gate self-clears within ~5s after turning OFF. manual_enabled left FALSE at end (verified via public status endpoint).

issues: Cookie consent banner overlaps the bottom of the Outage incidents card in default 1440x900 viewport; not a functional block but obscures last row. Cosmetic only.

critical_code_review_comments: MaintenanceGate EXEMPT_PREFIXES includes '/admin' — this means /admin/* routes always bypass the gate. Correct for the admin-must-be-able-to-recover use case, but also means the admin dashboard never sees the maintenance screen even for a non-admin user who somehow lands on an /admin/* URL. Acceptable since /admin/* is already server-side auth-gated.

Anon navigation to /dashboard results in a client-side redirect to /login?next=/dashboard BEFORE MaintenanceGate re-evaluates, so anon users on protected routes see the login form (exempt) rather than the maintenance screen. Public/landing routes (e.g. `/`) do correctly show the maintenance screen. This is fine given the design intent that /login must always be reachable, but worth noting: anon users going straight to auth-required URLs will see the sign-in form, not the maintenance overlay.
backend/services/maintenance.py `set_maintenance_state` always writes `updated_at`/`updated_by` even on a no-op call (empty body). Minor — harmless but bumps the cache timestamp on every call.

backend/services/maintenance.py `outage_stats` uses ISO-string comparison for the 30d cutoff; works because ISO 8601 UTC strings are lexically sortable, but is fragile if a naive/local-tz timestamp is ever inserted. Consider comparing on numeric `created_at_ts` for robustness.
test_credentials: test@aurem.dev / AuremTest2026! (admin/founder, preview env) — verified working via /api/aurem-dev/auth/login
seed_data_creation: None. All test settings written during testing (message/window/threshold=60, manual toggled ON then OFF) were cleared back to safe defaults at end. Confirmed manual_enabled=false on the public status endpoint at test completion.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Feature is stable and shipped. Backend pytest at /app/backend/tests/test_maintenance.py can be re-run as regression. Boot-gap auto-outage incident logging was NOT triggered (would require a supervisor restart with a stale heartbeat); shape/behavior of /admin/maintenance/incidents endpoint verified against empty dataset — schema is correct. If retesting, ensure you turn manual_enabled back OFF at end (test_zzz_final_ensure_manual_off does this automatically).
rca of the issue: N/A — no bugs found. The one bug the main agent self-identified and fixed (MaintenanceGate blocking /login for logged-out sessions) is confirmed fixed: /login and /signup render normally for anon visitors while manual=ON.
